citations.quote: Partial-word-2 shall consist of zero or one text-word
Partial-word-2 shall consist of zero or one text-word
any other sequence of contiguous COBOL characters bounded by separators
any other character or sequence of contiguous characters from the compile-time coded character set

cases.reason: Format 1 (LEADING/TRAILING partial-word) is identical in both editions, but the TERM the rule counts changed: a 2002 text-word (7.1.1.4 item 3) is a sequence of contiguous COBOL characters, a 2023 text-word (7.2.2.5 item 3) is any character sequence from the compile-time coded character set (the implementor may prohibit some). So in 2002 a partial-word-2 holding a character outside the COBOL repertoire (==Y¤Z==) is not zero or one text-word and violates SR6; in 2023 it is one text-word. The count part (two text-words refused, zero accepted) is shown at 2002 by rp-two.cob (COBOL2572) and rp-ok.cob (FOO BAR). The narrower 2002 text-word is not applied: rp-nonc.cob and rp-nonc3.cob compile clean at --std 2002, while word-nonc.cob shows the same compiler refuses U+00A4 in a COBOL word at 2002 (COBOL2773). Fifth cause: a text-manipulation term defined in 7.1.1.4 (not in clause 4) that 2023 widened; it reaches every pseudo-text / partial-word rule of 7.1.2 and 7.1.3.

partial-word-2: one text-word
partial-word-2: more than one text-word (refuse)
partial-word-2 containing a character outside the COBOL character repertoire (not a text-word in 2002: refuse)

cases.reason: The rule defers to "the rules of reference format", which differ: 2002 6.2.4 lets a COBOL word, a numeric literal or a picture character-string be broken across lines with a fixed continuation indicator; 2023 6.3.5 continues only alphanumeric, boolean and national literals. So 2002 SR8 also permits a COBOL word continued inside pseudo-text (and, via 2002 SR10, inside a debugging line within pseudo-text). Probe rp-cont.cob (word WORKAREA split inside pseudo-text-1) prints REPLACED at --std 2002 and is refused at --std 2023 (COBOL0902). Literal continuation inside pseudo-text behaves the same at both (rp-contlit.cob; 18 trailing spaces to margin R kept).
